The Petitioners have filed these three petitions under Sec.166 of Indian Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/ each for the injuries sustained by them in a road accident dated 08.03.2021.
All the petitions have arisen out of a common accident.
Therefore, all the petitions SCCH-25 have been clubbed together as per order dated 14.03.2024 for common trial and common judgment is passed.

2. The case of the Petitioners in brief is as follows: That on 08.03.2021 at about 3.45 pm the petitioner in MVC 7267/2022 was driving his Maruthi Omni bearing No.KA02MB2496 on Bangalore - Kanakapura Main Road along with his parents i.e., petitioners in MVC Nos.7268/20222 & 7269/2022, when they reached near Yaduvnahalli Gate, NH209 Road, Maralavadi Hobli, a Car bearing No.KA41C2326 driven by its driver with high speed in a rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life and dashed to the petitioners' vehicle.
Due to impact petitioners vehicle fully damaged and petitioners caught in the Car and also suffered grievous injuries.

3. It is the further case of the Petitioners in MVC Nos.7267/2022, 7268/2022 & 7269/2022 that,
SCCH-25 immediately after the accident they were taken to Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital, Kanakapura, wherein they were treated by spending Rs.20,000/ each towards their treatment.
The petitioner in MVC 7267/2022 was doing Business and the petitioners in MVC 7268/2022 & 7269/2022 were doing Agriculture work and each was earning Rs.30,000/ per month.
Due to accidental injuries they suffered financial loss.
The accident occurred due to the negligence of the offending Car Driver bearing Reg.No.KA41C 2326.
The Harohalli Police have registered a case against him.
The respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

4. In response to notice issued by this tribunal, the Respondent did not appear, hence placed ex parte.
5.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following Points:
SCCH-25 In MVC.7267/2022 1

Whether the Petitioner proves that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA41C2326 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries and his Maruthi Omni bearing NO.KA02MB2496 also damaged?
2.
Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom payable?

sentences.text: In order to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the Driver of the Car bearing Reg.No.KA41C2326, the petitioners have got examined themselves as PWs.1 to 3 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to 8.
They have reiterated the contents of the petition in their affidavits filed in lieu of chief examination.

10. The petitioner in MVC 7267/2022 has also got examined Mr. Madhukara - Proprietor of Fortune Motors as SCCH-25 PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.29 & 30 which are Notarized copy of his Aadhar Card and copy of GST certificate.

3 11.
The accident took place on 08.03.2021 and the FIR was registered on the complaint lodged by the relative of PW.1 on 30.04.2021 as per Ex.P.1.
Ex.P.2 is the spot mahazar.
The offending vehicle was seized on the same day of accident at about 4.30 to 5.00pm as per Ex.P.3.
Ex . P.4
is the statement of witnesses in the case.
It is in accordance with the statement given by the petitioners.
Ex.P.7 is the accused voluntary statement.
Ex . P.8
is the charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The wound Certificates at Exs.P.6, 17 & 23 show that the petitioners have suffered injuries in an RTA.

Therefore, on the basis of the documents before the court and the evidence of Pws.1 to 4 the court holds that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the Car bearing No.KA41C2326 SCCH-25 and petitioners' vehicle is also damaged.
Accordingly, Point No.1 in all the cases are held in the affirmative.
12. Point No.2 In MVC 7267/2022:
In order to prove the disability the petitioner has produced the wound certificate at Ex.P.6.
As per Ex.P.6 the petitioner has suffered abrasions on right leg, left knee joint and pain in right leg which are simple in nature.
He is suffering from pain and agony and also suffered financial loss due to the accidental injuries.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly SCCH-25 the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.6 discloses that, he has sustained simple injuries.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/
under the head of Pain and Suffering.

The Petitioner has stated that he has spent Rs.20,000/
towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc.,
In this regard he has produced medical bills for a sum of Rs.826/ at Ex.P.13.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital as an outpatient.
In this regard he has produced OPD Card at Ex.P.15.

During the treatment certainly he would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance,
transportation and for other incidental expenses.
Therefore, SCCH-25 the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.5,000/ towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other incidental expenses.
The petitioner has also averred that he has spent Rs.1,24,318/ for repair of his vehicle and also examined the Proprietor of the Fortune Motors in support of his case as PW.4.
The petitioner has produced the Invoices at Ex.P.16.
Therefore, he is entitled for the said amount under the head of repair expenses.
The total compensation comes to Rs.1,40,144/.

If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.1,40,200/.
13.

However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.23 discloses that, she has sustained simple injury.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/ under the head of Pain and Suffering.

In this regard she has produced medical bills for a sum of SCCH-25 Rs.398/ at Ex.25.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Dr.Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital as an inpatient.

If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.20,400/.
14.
Point No.2 In MVC 7269/2022:
In order to prove the disability he has produced the wound certificate at Ex.P.17.
As per Ex.P.17 the petitioner SCCH-25 has suffered Abrasion on back of left hand, back on head occipital region and back of left hand which are simple in nature.
He is suffering from pain and agony from the injuries suffered by him.

The Petitioner to substantiate that there is loss of income due to the accidental injuries and that he is suffering from disability has not examined either the treated Doctor or any other Doctor who has got expertise in this field.
He also has not placed any disability certificate issued by the competent person to prove that he suffered permanent disability.

Therefore, in absence of evidence this Tribunal holds that the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident has not caused him permanent disability resulting in loss of income and accordingly the version of the petitioner in this regard is not acceptable.
Under these circumstances the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of loss of future income due to disability.
However, it is pertinent to note that, the wound certificate produced as per Ex.P.17 SCCH-25 discloses that, he has sustained simple injury.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/ under the head of Pain and Suffering.
The Petitioner has stated that he has spent Rs.20,000/ towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc.,
In this regard he has produced medical bills for a sum of Rs.613/ at Ex.19.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled to the said amount under the head of medical expenses.
As mentioned above the Petitioner was treated at Dr. Chandramma Dayananda Sagar Hospital as an inpatient.
In this regard he has produced Discharge Summary issued by General Hospital, Kanakapura as per Exs.P.18.

As per Ex.P.18, it can be seen that the petitioner took treatment in the above said hospital from 08.03.2021 to 09.03.2021,
during that time certainly he would have spent some amount towards attendant, conveyance,
transportation and for other incidental expenses.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.10,000/ towards attendant, conveyance, transportation and other SCCH-25 incidental expenses.
The total compensation comes to Rs.20.613/.

LIABILITY
The respondent did not appear before the court and contest the matter.
The Petitioner in MVC No.7267/2022 has claimed a sum of Rs.5,00,000/, but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.1,40,200/ along with interest @ 6% pa..
The petitioner in MVC No.7268/2022 has claimed a sum of Rs.5,00,000/, but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.20,400/ along wtih interest @6% pa.
In the same manner Petitioner in MVC No.7269/2022 has claimed for a sum of Rs.5,00,000/, but he is entitled only for a sum of Rs.20,700/ along with interest @ 6% pa.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed.
Accordingly, Point No.2 in all the cases are held in the affirmative.
SCCH-25 16. Point No.3 in all the cases:

In view of above answers to the above Points, this court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER
The petitions in MVC No.7267/2022 to 7269/2022 are hereby allowed with cost.

The Petitioner in MVC. No.7267/2022 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.1,40,200/ (Rupees One Lakh Forty Thousand and Two Hundred only) along with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.

The Petitioner in MVC. No.7268/2022 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.20,400/ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Four Hundred only) along with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of SCCH-25 filing till the date of depositing the award amount.

The Petitioner in MVC. No.7269/2022 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.20,700/ (Rupees Twenty Thousand Seven Hundred only) along with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of filing till the date of depositing the award amount.
The Respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
On deposit of compensation and interest in all the cases, entire amount shall be released to the petitioners in their respective names by way of e payment with due acknowledgment and proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/ in each case.
SCCH-25
The original of this judgment is ordered to be kept in MVC.7267/2022 and the copy of it be kept in MVC.7268/2022 & 7269/2022.
